item.title: What a radical-pair quantum reservoir would require: readable capacity, no quantum advantage, and a nuclear-register criterion
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hikaru Wakaura, Taiki Tanimae
Whether the electron--nuclear spin coherence behind radical-pair magnetoreception could also support biological emphcomputation has been conjectured for decades but never made quantitative. We treat a cryptochrome-type radical pair as a reservoir computer, solving the radical-pair master equation with electronic decoherence and driving it as a real turnover does---by the birth of a spin-correlated pair whose singlet character encodes the input. Three results follow, none of them the expected one. item.title: Machine Learning and GIS-Integrated Framework for Irrigation Water Quality Index (IWQI) Mapping and Hydrochemical Clustering in an Algerian Semi-Arid Watershed
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Zahra Benkhamallah, Bachir Hallouche, Khaled Korichi
In the Ain Temouchent region, surface water is severely limited, leaving groundwater as the primary source for both domestic supply and agricultural irrigation. This study evaluates the suitability of El Melah watershed groundwater for irrigation by computing the Irrigation Water Quality Index (IWQI) following the Meireles approach, mapping its spatial distribution through GIS, and complementing the analysis with two machine learning methods: (i) a Random Forest (RF) model with Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) and SHAP explainability analysis to identify the dominant drivers of IWQI degradation; and (ii) K-means and hierarchical clustering to delineate hydrochemical facies and provide a statistically grounded alternative to the conventional Wilcox diagram. item.title: Eichhornia crassipes management in a eutrophic reservoir: Cover reduction, rapid recolonization, and cyanobacterial dynamics
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Daniel H. C. Salim¹, Caio C. S. Mello¹, Gabriel Pereira², Raian V. Maretto³, Camila C. Amorim¹
Mechanical harvesting is widely used to control Eichhornia crassipes in reservoirs, yet its performance is judged by biomass removed rather than the reduction and stabilization of plant cover. We integrated a 129 month Sentinel-1 time series derived using U-Net segmentation with harvesting records and water quality monitoring to evaluate harvest campaigns, recurrent expansion and phytoplankton responses in a 177 ha eutrophic tropical urban reservoir. Harvesting effort was not proportional to cover change: campaigns with comparable biomass removal produced contrasting outcomes. Cover reductions were followed by recolonization, with the two fastest episodes doubling reservoir scale cover in 19 and 20 days. item.title: Audience evaluation of heritage-derived cultural-creative products: a multilevel analysis of rater-level and product-level variance
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Zetian Wang, Fangming Zhao, Wentao Tang, Mingfeng Xiao, Lingling Zheng
Studies of heritage-derived cultural-creative products often interpret audience ratings as differences between products, yet each rating also reflects the person who gives it. This study examined how these two sources of variance contribute to evaluations of six designs derived from the Wa jicong top, a spinning top from Yunnan, China. Each of 228 respondents rated two randomly assigned designs, giving 456 evaluations. Crossed random-effects models estimated the rater and product shares of each response, and within-rater and between-rater analyses separated two kinds of association among evaluative judgements. item.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Aleksandr Shlykov, Meissa L. Diouf, Richard Karl, Mikolaj Roguski, Umesh C. Joshi, Stefan Willitsch
Nature Communications, Published online: 31 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78680-w The authors report the control of electric quadrupole rovibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic spectroscopy protocol. This allows identification of hyperfine components of the fundamental vibrational transition of N2+ ions and coherent population transfer.

item.title: The general Stokes’ theorem as the mechanism for synchronizing 2s2p electrons within a neon atom
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Kunming Xu
Points, arcs, surfaces, and solids are four orthogonal space dimensions of a sphere. When they are applied to the description of the atomic structure of a neon shell, we draw the conclusion that both full-fledged 2px electronic orbitals manifest as two diametric points; both 2py orbitals take the shape of two semicircular arcs; both 2pz orbitals spread over two hemispherical surfaces; and both 2s orbitals form a solid spherical layer. The electrons transform from one type of orbitals to another cyclically following dynamic calculus of spherical quantities rather than linear algebra of physical quantities. item.title: Development and Experimental Validation of a Dual-Input Dual-Output DC-DC Converter for PV–Battery Hybrid Energy Systems
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Saber Zare, Amirhossein Rajaei, Mohammad Karimianfard
Due to the inherently fluctuating nature of renewable energy sources, their output current and voltage exhibit significant intermittency, rendering them insufficient for standalone sustainable power delivery. To address this, hybrid systems combining renewables with auxiliary storage or generation units are commonly deployed. This study introduces an innovative dual-input dual-output (DIDO) DC-DC converter configuration utilizing a T-source impedance network. In the proposed setup, a photovoltaic (PV) array and a battery storage unit serve as the dual input ports. The converter is controlled such that the battery compensates for any power deficits when the PV output falls short of the load requirements, whereas excess PV generation is directed to charge the battery during surplus periods.…
